_meta.description: Screen Awareness (Phase 2 'Seeing') known-mistake reference for Blender, first-slice scope. Each entry is a real, verifiable Fallout 4 export/pipeline mistake a screenshot of Blender's viewport/outliner/properties panel can plausibly reveal. Sent to the vision recognition pass as a compact reference of what Mossy already knows to check for -- NOT the full knowledge base, just this narrow slice's patterns. New entries only get added here via ChangeGate's approve() -- see change_gate.py -- never edited by hand as a shortcut around review.

patterns.whatToLookFor: UV Editing workspace or the mesh's UV Map data shows no unwrap (a single default square UV, or the UV Maps list in Object Data Properties is empty) on a mesh that has a material with an image texture assigned.
patterns.correction: A mesh exported without a real UV unwrap will show correct geometry in-game but garbled or stretched textures -- unwrap (U > Unwrap or Smart UV Project) before assigning textures, not after.

patterns.whatToLookFor: Expecting a slower/softer wind preset (e.g. Kelp / Seaweed underwater current) to change how a plant moves in Fallout 4 by setting a wind 'amplitude' or 'period'. FO4 vegetation wind speed and timing are global engine settings; amplitude/period values stored on the Blender object never reach the NIF, so an underwater preset exported identical to a land plant.
patterns.correction: The only per-mesh control over sway strength is the exported vertex alpha (VERTEX_ALPHA, 0 = anchored, 1 = full sway). For underwater plants cap it: Kelp/Seaweed about 50%, soft coral about 35%. Use the add-on's 'Underwater: Kelp / Seaweed' or 'Soft Coral' buttons (they now scale the alpha and remember it for re-bakes). Rigid/stony coral should use No Wind.

patterns.whatToLookFor: An object already modelled in FO4 game units but smaller than 20 units on every axis (small props, sponges, cans) gets multiplied by 70 on export by the add-on's 'untagged object = metres' guess, producing a NIF 70x too big. Separately, exporting an object tagged fo4_unit_scale=1.0 used to leave it shrunk to 1/70 in the scene afterwards.
patterns.correction: Tag game-unit objects with the custom property fo4_unit_scale = 1.0 before exporting so the metre heuristic is skipped. The add-on's export now restores each object by the exact factor it was scaled up by, so the scene size stays the same after export.
